name: ADR 0002 - V2 greenfield reset, v1 archived in git only
description: V1 ingestion code is frozen git-only; the active tree is rebuilt from scratch with per-tool parsers proven by golden tests before any DB write.
content:
# ADR 0002 - V2 greenfield reset, v1 archived in git only

## Status
Accepted (2026-06-08).

## Context
V1 ingestion was wrong in ways documented in plan 00 (probe0 db findings) and plan 01 (problem and goals). The unit of work was the file/container, the only change primitive was a whole-file fingerprint (path_hash + size + mtime), and message identity was positional (session_id, sequence_number). For append-only JSONL and in-place-mutated SQLite (opencode.db) the bytes move on every run, so "incremental" degenerated into full reprocess gated by a check the important files fail every time. Worse, identity was a write-layer choice that discarded native ids OpenCode already carried (0.0% null, 100% distinct). Retrofitting v1 merge logic cannot fix capture semantics.

## Decision
1. V1 ingestion (parsers, pipeline, storage, schema, deployment docs) lives only in git at tag legacy-v1-file-parser-freeze-2026-08, branch archive/v1-file-parser, commit 28c936a. The active tree carries no v1 modules in src/.
2. What stays in the tree: plans 00-06, source dossiers, TOOL_AUDIT, tests/fixtures, tools/ YAMLs, ingestion_v2/, and the parked corpus-canonical inventory.
3. G-0 stream taxonomy (ingestion_v2/stream_taxonomy.py) classifies artifacts before projection; only conversation_transcript and subagent_transcript may create projected messages.
4. Build order: read real source files -> document patterns -> golden tests -> per-tool parsers -> schema on clone -> corpus load last. No production DB until parsers are proven on fixtures and clone rehearsal.

## Consequences
- The CLI ships only --discover today; ingest, init-db, doctor, and daemon exit with a not-wired message.
- schema/base.sql and v1 migrations are recoverable via `git show archive/v1-file-parser:schema/base.sql` for forensics only.
- No client-side encryption, no client-side PII scrubbing, no v1 code copies in src/.
- The canonical corpus dump is parked and hands-off until parsers pass golden tests and clone rehearsal (see ADR 0003).

name: ADR 0001 - Parser-native raw records before projections
description: Make tool-native raw records the system of record and chat_sessions/messages derived projections rebuilt from them; anchor identity to native ids before any cursor or corpus work.
content:
# ADR 0001 - Parser-native raw records before projections

## Status
Accepted (2026-06-08). Kill-gate removed; the cheap Phase 0 conditional-upsert mitigation is recast as a headroom measure, not an alternative.

## Context
In v1, chat_sessions and messages were simultaneously the system of record and the queryable view, and identity was positional. v1 jsonl_parser re-sorted messages by timestamp and storage assigned sequence_number by enumerate, so equal or missing timestamps caused sequence drift and mis-attribution across runs. v1 jsonl_parser also silently dropped messages with a duplicate (role, content, timestamp) triple that lacked an external_id - lossy for repeated short messages. The motivating use case is code-and-conversation forensics, which requires a message to keep a stable identity across runs so "session X wrote openclaw.json at time T" stays a fixed, citable fact.

## Decision
Split the roles. A raw layer preserves tool-native evidence verbatim (native id, source artifact, raw payload, content hash) and is the only thing a cursor advances over; it is never re-keyed by a later parse. chat_sessions and messages become projections rebuilt deterministically from the raw layer. The raw layer is two tables: raw_record_keys (one stable identity row per logical record, forever) and raw_record_revisions (immutable, append-only, row-hashed content history). Capture happens BEFORE any lossy normalization - the pre-merge iter_raw_records() contract is a blocking pre-schema deliverable. Message identity is anchored to native source-local ids where present, with explicit (source_artifact, position)+row-hash fallback where absent, across three tiers (T1 have it / T2 partial / T3 synthesize). Sequence this BEFORE cursors, schema, or corpus load - otherwise we make the flawed model faster instead of correct.

## Consequences
- The full-container fingerprint (source_file_state) is demoted to an optional cold-file fast-path hint, not deleted.
- messages.raw_record_key_id binds each projected row to its raw identity so messages.id (and embeddings) never re-attach to a different record (F1 identity-map invariant). N->1 composition (Kilo, Kimi, OpenCode) is tracked in a message_raw_records lineage table, not a single FK.
- Content hashing is a deliberate, scoped reversal of v1's no-content-hash stance: row_hash is a change-detection hash on raw records, not the dedup key.
- Downstream consumers (messages.id, embeddings, content_tsvector, chat_sessions.metadata cwd, audit_status) must keep working; the migration is non-destructive and additive.

name: ADR 0003 - Canonical dump parked until clone rehearsal passes
description: The 2.49GB v1 corpus pg_dump is the single authoritative frozen snapshot; no production restore, migration, or ingest until parsers pass golden tests and a clone rehearsal on a throwaway DB.
content:
# ADR 0003 - Canonical dump parked until clone rehearsal passes

## Status
Accepted (2026-06-08).

## Context
The corpus is irreplaceable: source files rotate, so a lost or corrupted row cannot be recovered from the origin. A canonical pg_dump of the v1 corpus was taken at the greenfield reset boundary (D:\llm-archiver-archive\llm_archival_20260608_020001.sql.gz, ~2.49GB, gzip integrity verified). The committed global Probe 2 was invalid as a no-op gate - its "NO-OP" run still wrote +9,611 message updates, +1,162 provenance inserts, and 204MB WAL because live sources grow between runs. The migration is the highest-risk part of the rework (G3 corpus durability governs).

## Decision
The canonical dump is parked and hands-off. Until v2 parsers pass golden tests and clone rehearsal:
- No pg_restore against production.
- No migration apply against production.
- No production ingest against the live corpus URI.
Active work is fixture and contract tests only. Clone rehearsal uses a throwaway DB restored from the canonical dump. Before any production write: restore the canonical dump to a separate database, record row counts and smoke queries. The cutover is shadow -> fidelity-tagged backfill -> flip, gated on TWO human-reviewed diffs (content diff and identity-map diff), not auto-accepted. Migrations 010-017 are additive and idempotent; the only allowed destructive action is the enumerated corrective re-key path for the known 66 spliced rows and #93 re-stitches, after restore and staging evidence exist.

## Consequences
- Production writes stay off until verified restore/PITR, real-corpus staging rehearsal, and the audited corrective re-key manifest all exist.
- Backfill is forward-only by default and fidelity-tagged (source_reconcile / projection_backfill / projected_only); projection_backfill rows are flagged lossy, excluded from source-coverage metrics, and never advance a cursor.
- Every backfill change is recorded in projection_backfill_audit (old_values/new_values/run_id) so rollback is mechanized; no sequence_number or content is changed before the flip.
- Server-side destructive-statement auditing stays on; the ~690 orphan source_file_state rows from #93 are re-checked and either linked or explained, never guessed.
